title: PhysxCollisionAPI
summary: PhysX contact tuning for a collision shape. Offsets use a value sentinel instead of the authored bit because ovstage reports every column as authored.
producer_scope: Every declared attribute is published at its resolved value. The only derivation is contactOffset on a Plane collider (0.02 / metersPerUnit when unauthored). For every other shape the raw -inf fallbacks of contactOffset and restOffset reach the consumer, which treats them as unset through its value sentinel. The producer documents the non-plane -1 auto sentinel and the Newton contactMargin/contactGap cascade as unimplemented.

columns.name: physxCollision:contactOffset

producer.notes: On a Plane collider only, whether or not it applies PhysxCollisionAPI. Every other shape keeps the schema fallback -inf.

verify.notes: Absent means computed from shape size; only the authored value is checked.

columns.absent: -1, meaning the PhysX layer computes the offset from shape size. Writing the raw fallback -inf is equivalent to omitting the column.
columns.sentinel: value < -0.5e38 means unset (same as absent); +inf means authored auto (-1); finite is authored and clamped to [0, FLT_MAX]
columns.notes: Automatic contact offset is preserved until the runtime computes the distance from shape size and adds any positive rest offset. A concrete contact offset is committed only when contactOffset >= restOffset. For a plane shape the absent default is instead 0.02 / metersPerUnit.

columns.name: physxCollision:restOffset
columns.absent: 0 for a collider, 0.02 / metersPerUnit for a deformable body. An authored rest offset is preserved when contact offset is automatic. With a concrete contact offset, colliders require restOffset < contactOffset; deformable bodies accept restOffset <= contactOffset, with equality diagnosed and the contact offset increased during shape creation.
columns.sentinel: value < -0.5e38 means unset; +inf means authored 0; finite is authored
